title: Yu Hae-ran posts 5-under to tie for third at BMW Ladies Championship in Korea - CHOSUNBIZ
text:
Yu Hae-ran posts 5-under to tie for third at BMW Ladies Championship in Korea - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 23일(금) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Yu Hae-ran posts 5-under to tie for third at BMW Ladies Championship in Korea 
 입력 2026.10.22. 16:50 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Yu Hae-ran (25) defended the host nation's pride in the first round of the LPGA tournament held in Korea, 'BMW Ladies Championship 2026 (BMW Ladies Championship 2026)'.
 Yu Hae-ran, in the first round of the BMW Ladies Championship 2026 (total purse $2.35 million = about 3.1 billion won, winner's prize $352,500 = about 470 million won), which opened on the 22nd at Pine Beach Golf Links (par 72/6,784 yards) in Haenam County, Gwangju Metropolitan City, Jeollanam-do, recorded five birdies and no bogeys to finish tied for third.
 She made three birdies on the front nine and two on the back nine, and on the par-4 5th hole a chip shot near the green rolled straight into the cup, earning applause from the gallery.
 In a postround interview, Yu Hae-ran said, "It was a bit tough because the wind blew more than I expected early on, but I was able to finish relatively smoothly by recalling the practice I did yesterday. Windy courses are still difficult. Thanks to consecutive birdies on holes 5 and 6 on the front nine I was able to keep a good rhythm, but it's a little disappointing that I missed a birdie putt chance near the end. On the back nine, I think I was rewarded with consecutive birdies on holes 15 and 16 because I held on well during the stretch of pars."
 About the remaining rounds, she said, "Today felt like a really good day. But the weekend weather could be a variable, so I'll play well tomorrow and think about the remaining rounds later. My father's neighborhood is near this course so many people came to cheer, and I expect many more to come over the next three days."
 Four players crowded the 5-under group that included Yu Hae-ran. America's Lucy Lee, Lauren Koglin and Spain's Julia Lopez Ramirez formed the tied-for-third group.
 At 6 under, Australia's Charis Davidson and Japan's Yoshida Yuri led. Davidson made eight birdies on Pine Beach's tricky course but also had two bogeys, while Yoshida Yuri recorded six birdies and no bogeys.
 Korea's Kim Hyo-joo, Kim Min-seon, Yang Hee-young and Kim Min-ju formed a tied-for-eighth group at 3 under.
 Strong winds continued around Pine Beach during the first round, following the previous day. Compared with the 21st the wind had died down somewhat, but tee shots on the par-3 holes with elevation changes were greatly affected by the wind.
